candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed pp.38-39: provide client education about medications; monitor anticipated medication interactions and adverse effects; evaluate client response to medication.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — disulfiram safety teaching and alcohol interaction
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients taking disulfiram to avoid alcoholic beverages and hidden alcohol in foods, medicines, and topical products, including during the labeled period when alcohol reactions can still occur after the last dose.

options.A: Avoid alcoholic beverages, but alcohol-containing foods and medicines do not need to be checked.
options.B: Avoid alcoholic beverages and alcohol in disguised forms, including alcohol-containing foods, medicines, and topical products.
options.C: Avoid alcohol only for 24 hours after the final disulfiram dose, then resume usual alcohol-containing products.
options.D: Avoid alcohol-containing foods, but alcohol-containing cough medicines and topical products are acceptable.

candidate.rationale: Current DailyMed labeling instructs patients taking disulfiram to avoid alcohol, including alcohol in disguised forms such as sauces, vinegars, cough mixtures, aftershave lotions, and back rubs. The label also warns that a disulfiram-alcohol reaction may occur with alcohol up to 14 days after ingesting disulfiram. Therefore B is correct. A and D fail to account for labeled hidden sources of alcohol. C incorrectly shortens the labeled post-disulfiram risk period to 24 hours.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Disulfiram patients should avoid beverage alcohol and hidden alcohol sources such as certain foods, medicines, and topical products; alcohol reactions can occur for up to 14 days after disulfiram ingestion.
candidate.source_locator: Warnings: avoid alcohol in disguised forms, including sauces, vinegars, cough mixtures, aftershave lotions, and back rubs; reactions may occur with alcohol up to 14 days after ingesting disulfiram. Clinical Pharmacology: alcohol ingestion one or even two weeks after the last dose may produce unpleasant symptoms.
candidate.stem: A client starting disulfiram asks which products should be avoided. Which teaching is correct?
